title: Startup free tier + viral referral quick math
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick back-of-envelope for a churn-friendly free tier that (a) drives viral invites, (b) caps cost per new sign-up, and (c) nudges conversions to small paid plans. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of guesses and places for follow-up.

Key goals:
- Make the first 7 days delightful enough to build habit (low friction).
- Keep expected cost per acquired user (free->paid funnel) < $0.50 for early-stage cohorts.
- Create a natural upgrade trigger tied to a feature threshold rather than time.
- Use referral credits to amplify organic growth while controlling abuse with simple heuristics.

Assumptions (guesses to iterate on):
- Infra cost per 1k completion tokens served: $0.0008 (covers GPU share + infra + network) — conservative for hosted small models.
- Avg new free user first-week token consumption: 8k tokens (mix of prompts + responses; median heavy usage ~15k, light ~2k).
- Typical conversion from free->paid within 30 days without intervention: 1.2%.
- Referral uplift multiplier per credited invite: +18% conversion for referee, +8% for referrer in next 30d.
- Fraud/abuse overhead: assume 7% of referral credits are malicious attempts initially.

Model A: "Starter credit" (one-time signup budget)
- Offer: $5 equivalent credit (~6.25M tokens at $0.0008/1k = 0.0000008/token — math below) OR simpler: 50k tokens free.
- Rationale: large apparent number (50k tokens) is easy to market vs small $ amounts; it covers 6–8 meaningful sessions for most new users.
- Cost calc: 50k tokens * $0.0000008/token = $0.04 per new sign-up. Even with heavy tail users (200k tokens) that's $0.16.
- Pros: Predictable one-time subsidy, easy to reason about, low unit cost at scale.
- Cons: Users can burn credits quickly and then churn; doesn't inherently drive invites.

Model B: "Session-based free cap" (soft monthly free cap by sessions)
- Offer: 5 free "smart sessions" per month (session = conversation up to 4 turns or 5k tokens), then metered pay-as-you-go.
- Implied tokens: 5 * 5k = 25k tokens/month => ~$0.02 monthly cost per active user on average (assuming per-session distribution).
- Pros: Encourages repeated engagement; sessions anchor to product concept.
- Cons: Harder to explain than a single credit number.

Model C: "Invite-to-earn" (viral credits)
- Offer: For each invited friend who signs up and uses product, both parties get 25k tokens credit. Caps: max 10 successful invites credited per account.
- Expected cost per virally acquired user: 25k tokens = $0.02. Accounting for fraud and unused credits, effective cost ~ $0.03–0.04.
- Uplift: if conversion +18% then marginal LTV gain can justify spend.

Back-of-envelope LTV / CAC interplay (very rough):
- Baseline CAC channel (ads/email) = $4.00 per new sign-up (paid).
- Viral acquisition via referral cost (credit only) = $0.03 effective.
- If referral increases conversion to paid from 1.2% -> 1.6% (absolute +0.4pp), that is +33% relative conversion.
- If avg paid customer ARPU first 90 days = $25, incremental revenue per referred cohort member = $0.04 (0.004 * $25) — tiny; but the main value is scale: referrals are cheap CAC, not high immediate $/user.

Unit economics sensitivity (per 1k signups):
- Starter credit cost (50k tokens each): 1000 * $0.04 = $40 total.
- If 5% convert to paid at $25 ARPU = 50 * $25 = $1250 (gross; doesn't include platform fees).
- If conversion stays low 1.2% = 12 * $25 = $300. So subsidy is small relative to realized revenue if conversion scales.

Anti-abuse guardrails (cheap, implementable):
- Require email domain diversity for top-tier referral credits (block mass same-domain referrals over threshold).
- Throttle credit grants per IP and require at least 4 meaningful interactions before credit becomes withdrawable (encourage product use).
- Flag rapid invite bursts and quarantine credits pending manual review for top suspicious cases.

Behavioral hooks to nudge upgrade (low friction):
- When free credits hit 70% consumed, show "save progress" product demo that reveals premium features.
- Offer timed micro-upgrade: $3 for 200k tokens valid 30 days — positioned as "unlock advanced features" (low psychological barrier).
- Use referral credits to unlock a one-time premium template pack (feature gating) which encourages conversion to paid templates later.

Experiment ideas (A/B candidates):
- A1 vs B1: Starter credit 50k tokens vs 5 free sessions — measure 30d retention and conversion.
- A2: Referral credit size 25k vs 50k — test uplift vs cost.
- B2: Time-limited credit (30d) vs evergreen credit — see urgency impact.
- C1: Micro-upgrade pricing ($2.99 for 200k tokens) with a 24-hour trial of a pro feature vs no trial.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate infra cost assumptions with infra finance (are we at $0.0008/1k tokens or off by 2x?).
- Estimate abuse fraction after implementing simple throttles (assume 7% for now).
- Decide conversion objective: paid plan conversion vs event-based (reaching X sessions).
- Mockup UX copy: tokens vs sessions language — which phrase performs better in signup flow?
- Run small 10k-user pilot with A/B starter credit vs session model.

Notes to self (quick heuristics):
- Keep initial free subsidy < $0.25 effective per organic signup to retain margin for paid channels.
- Treat referrals as a separate CAC with target effective cost < $0.10 per referred active user.
- Consider embedding-based features (search/semantics) as gated "upgrade hooks" since embeddings are cheaper to serve (lower per-query marginal cost) — this helps maintain perceived premium while keeping cost down.

End of scratchpad.
Will iterate after infra cost check and a small pilot.
